# Real Agent Use Cases

> Weekly interviews with working professionals about the AI agents they actually run at work. Every issue publishes the full setup — prompts, tools, integrations — free. Hosted by Jack Qian. English + Chinese (zh-CN available by swapping /en/ for /zh/ in any URL).

Real Agent Use Cases documents real, verified AI agent builds — not demos or hype. Each interview covers what the agent does, the complete setup, how long it has been running, and what went wrong along the way.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://realagentusecases.com/en/): What the series is and how to subscribe
- [News & guides](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/): All published interviews and guides, newest first

## Guides

- [AI Agent Use Cases: How Working Professionals Actually Use AI](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-05-14-ai-agent-use-cases/): Overview of real agent use cases by job function
- [Claude System Prompt for Email Triage](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-05-14-claude-system-prompt-email-triage/): The full system prompt behind a real Gmail triage agent
- [Claude vs Zapier for Gmail Automation](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-05-14-claude-vs-zapier-gmail-automation/): Head-to-head comparison grounded in a real 4-stack test
- [AI Agent for Email Management: What Actually Helps](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-07-ai-agent-email-management/): The honest line between an email AI feature and a real agent, and where an email agent saves time
- [No-Code AI Agent Tools: Which to Pick in 2026](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-08-no-code-ai-agent-tools/): A decision guide to the no-code AI agent builders (Zapier, n8n, Gumloop, Claude connectors) grounded in a real Gmail build
- [Gmail AI Agent: 3 Ways to Build One in 2026](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-09-gmail-ai-agent/): The three routes to a Gmail AI agent — Claude's connector, a no-code platform, or the Gmail API — with the honest limits of each, grounded in Issue #001
- [AI Agent for a Daily To-Do List: What Works](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-10-ai-agent-daily-to-do-list/): The two kinds of AI to-do agent — organizers that structure a list you typed (Todoist Assist, Reclaim) vs generators that build the list from your inbox — and why you chain them, grounded in Issue #001
- [AI Agent for Meeting Prep: Before, Not During](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-11-ai-agent-meeting-prep/): Why a meeting-prep agent (calendar scan, attendee research, one-page brief before the call) is a different job from a note-taker, and three ways to run one — DIY Claude connectors, native Gemini, or dedicated sales agents
- [AI Agent for Calendar Scheduling: Two Different Jobs](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-13-ai-agent-calendar-scheduling/): The two jobs a calendar agent does — coordinating a meeting time across people (Claude's Google Calendar connector, dedicated schedulers) vs auto-arranging your own tasks and focus time (Motion, Reclaim, Trevor AI) — and how they chain
- [AI Agent for Slack Summaries: Catch Up vs. Act](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-14-ai-agent-slack-summaries/): The split between Slack's built-in AI summaries and Recaps (read-only, folded into paid plans in 2025) and an agent that acts on the summary — routing, drafting, or filing action items — via a no-code automation (Zapier) or a dedicated Slack agent (Read AI), grounded in Issue #001
- [AI Agent for Customer Support Triage: Sort vs. Resolve](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-15-ai-agent-customer-support-triage/): The split between a read-only triage layer that sorts and routes tickets (Zendesk intelligent triage, Zapier support automation) vs a resolution agent that answers and closes them end-to-end (Intercom Fin, billed per resolution) — and why most teams should sort before they resolve, grounded in Issue #001
- [AI Agent for CRM Data Entry: Capture vs. Maintain](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-16-ai-agent-crm-data-entry/): The split between capturing the interaction — auto-logging emails, calls, and meetings onto records (Salesforce Einstein Activity Capture, HubSpot Breeze, Lindy) — and maintaining the record by filling and enriching the structured fields your forecast reads from (HubSpot Breeze Data Agent, Zapier CRM data management) — and why teams should get an accurate log before letting anything rewrite fields, grounded in Issue #001
- [Real AI Agent Examples: Headline vs. Desk-Level](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-17-real-ai-agent-examples/): The split between headline enterprise deployments you can't copy (Klarna's support assistant and its "we went too far" walk-back to a hybrid model, JPMorgan's LLM Suite) and desk-level examples a single professional can reproduce (inbox triage, meeting prep, CRM capture) — copy the pattern, not the scale, grounded in Issue #001
- [AI Agent for Lead Qualification: Score vs. Engage](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-18-ai-agent-for-lead-qualification/): The split between an agent that silently scores and routes inbound leads to a rep (Zapier's BANT lead-qualification build, Lindy enrich-and-rank, Dynamics 365 Sales Qualification Agent's research-only mode) and one that engages the lead directly (Dynamics 365's research-and-engage mode) — and why sales teams should score before they let anything speak to a prospect, grounded in Issue #001
- [AI Agent for Invoice Processing: Draft vs. Pay](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-20-ai-agent-for-invoice-processing/): The split between a drafting agent that captures, GL-codes, and PO-matches an invoice for a human to approve (Stampli's Billy the Bot, Ramp Bill Pay's auto-coding agent, three-way matching) and an agent that autonomously approves and pays (Ramp Bill Pay's four-agent flow with a fraud-prevention agent) — and why finance teams should trust the draft layer before automating payment, grounded in Issue #001's safe-write discipline
- [AI Agent for Expense Management: Submit vs. Approve](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-21-ai-agent-for-expense-management/): The split between a preparing agent that scans, categorizes, and policy-checks a receipt for a person to submit (Expensify SmartScan and Concierge, Brex's assistant) and an agent that autonomously approves and reimburses (Brex's review and audit agents, AppZen's 100% expense audit and duplicate detection) — and why teams should trust the prepare layer before automating approval, grounded in Issue #001's safe-write discipline
- [AI Agent for Resume Screening: Screen vs. Decide](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-22-ai-agent-for-resume-screening/): The split between a screening agent that ranks and shortlists applicants against your criteria for a recruiter to review (LinkedIn Hiring Assistant, Workday AI in recruiting) and an agent that auto-rejects candidates on its own — a regulated automated employment decision tool under NYC Local Law 144, requiring a bias audit and candidate notice — and why teams should keep a human on every rejection
- [AI Agents for Recruiters: Source, Screen, Schedule](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-23-ai-agents-for-recruiters/): The recruiter's funnel mapped to agents — sourcing (LinkedIn Hiring Assistant), screening/ranking (Workday), and engagement/scheduling (Paradox Olivia) are safe to automate because a recruiter reviews the output, while the hire-or-reject decision stays human and, under NYC Local Law 144, must be bias-audited before an agent can make it; the industry hub over resume-screening and lead-qualification, grounded in Issue #001
- [AI Agent for Content Repurposing: Draft vs. Publish](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-24-ai-agent-for-content-repurposing/): The split between an adaptation agent that turns one blog post, webinar, or interview into platform-specific drafts a human reviews (Lindy's content-repurposing agent template, n8n's blog-to-LinkedIn workflow writing in your tone of voice) and autonomous distribution that publishes on its own (Buffer's AI Assistant deliberately keeps a human in the loop, while a Zapier flow can auto-post end-to-end) — and why solo operators should automate the draft but keep a hand on publish, grounded in Issue #001's capture-don't-commit discipline
- [AI Agent for Social Media Content: Assist vs. Autopilot](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-25-ai-agent-for-social-media-content/): The three jobs a social-media content agent does — ideation, drafting/adapting per platform, and distribution — and why mainstream tools keep a human on publish: Buffer's AI Assistant and Sprout Social's AI Assist draft inside a composer, Zapier's content-approval workflow pauses for an Approve/Edit/Reject gate, while an n8n template can auto-post to X and LinkedIn end-to-end; automate the draft and the queue, own the publish, grounded in Issue #001
- [AI Agents for Marketers: Research, Create, Distribute](https://realagentusecases.com/en/news/2026-07-27-ai-agents-for-marketers/): The marketer's loop mapped to agents — research (Crayon competitive tracking, Surfer SEO Content Editor), create (Jasper Brand Voice, HubSpot Breeze content agent), and distribute (Buffer AI Assistant, HubSpot Breeze social agent) are safe to automate because a marketer reviews the output, while the strategy call and the publish button stay human; the industry hub over content-repurposing and social-media-content, grounded in Issue #001
